findings: Solved 2026-10-30 on the owner's request (exercises book by book, in Practice): Chapter 6 exercise as printed on PDF 140-143 (printed pages 140-143), in the book's words and order; headings as printed (Multiple Choice Questions, Short-Answer Questions, Descriptive Questions, Numerical Problems).
Counts: 12 MCQs (Q.1 I-XII), 12 short questions (Q.2 a-l), 2 descriptive questions (Q.3, Q.4), 6 numerical problems (Q.5-Q.10); all solved in English and Roman Urdu.

The book prints no answer key. MCQ keys worked out from the chapter: I b, II d, III c, IV a, V c, VI c, VII d, VIII c, IX c, X c, XI c, XII b. MCQ VIII keyed by the chapter's cycle (6.9.3): Delta H latt + Delta H sol = Delta H hyd, so Delta H sol = -Delta H latt + Delta H hyd.

Book corrections (boxes): MCQ I and II options print no arrow between reactants and products (a blank gap), -> written in; Q.5 has part (a) only; Q.6 equations print the arrow after the product; Q.8 table prints the ionization step as K(s) -> K+(g) + e- (should be K(g)), and lacks state symbols for KBr(s), Br(g), Br-(g); Q.10 repeats Sample Problem 6.12.

Numericals (the book prints no answers): Q.5 q(water) = 100.0 x 4.18 x 1.03 = 431 J, Delta H = -43.1 kJ mol-1 (NaOH 0.0100 mol); Q.6 -159.05 kJ mol-1; Q.7 -277.8 kJ mol-1; Q.8 lattice energy KBr -672 kJ mol-1; Q.9 Delta S surroundings = +4262 J K-1 mol-1 (+4.26 kJ K-1 mol-1); Q.10 Delta H = -17.8 kJ, Delta S = -144.7 J/K, Delta G = +25.3 kJ, non-spontaneous, agreeing with Sample Problem 6.12.

Table-based Q8: the printed table is given in words in the prompt. Q.4 Born-Haber cycle of NaCl uses the chapter's Figure 6.9 values (+108, +496, +121, -349, Delta Hf -411; Delta Hx 376; lattice -787 kJ mol-1); the cycle is described in words, no figure added.

Definitions follow the chapter, except the enthalpy of hydration in Short e(ii), defined for one mole of gaseous ions (the chapter's wording reads 'one mole of a solute'), with the chapter's example value for Na+ (-406 kJ mol-1, Sample Problem 6.8). Short e(iv) uses the chapter's -1368 kJ mol-1 for ethanol (Q.7 prints -1367).
Comparison answers (Short a, c, d) carry two-column answer tables. Draft for the academic review.
